storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Come settle in for The Parade That Tiptoed.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Hold up your hands like a parade conductor. Can you show us a beat without making a sound?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> My hands can march right here!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip lifted a yellow horn. The sidewalk parade began.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Stomp, clap, toot!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Stomp, clap, toot! Ms. Lily opened her blue gate.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Could you go softly here? My baby is napping.”

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <gasp> Bea’s hands stopped right there.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Can we keep the beat with one tiny finger step?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes. Let one finger take a tiny step on your knee while the baby naps.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip tucked the horn under one arm. “Can our parade go on tiptoe?”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Bea tried one tiny step. “It can!”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip took another tiny step. Bea patted her knees.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Then they both waved. Tiptoe, pat, wave!

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: One, two. Now I’ll count the next steps on my fingers.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Can you lead us in order? Which move comes after tiptoe?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: A soft knee pat. <giggle> Then I’ll finish with my biggest silent wave!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: That’s it. Lead us with a tiptoe, a soft pat, and a wave.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Ms. Lily smiled at the gate. Pip waved her over.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: She stepped out and fell in beside Bea. Tiptoe, pat, wave!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: They tiptoed past the nap window. The curtain didn’t stir. <sigh>

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Ms. Lily whispered, “Still asleep.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: At the end of the block, they stopped for one last wave. Ms. Lily waved with both hands.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Pip grinned so wide that Bea grinned, too. <chuckle>

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Ms. Lily used both hands! How did tiptoe, pat, and wave help her baby sleep?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Their feet and pats were soft, and their waves made no sound. The baby got to keep napping.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Let’s conduct those last three moves together.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Tiptoe, then pat your knees softly.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: <giggle> Now give the baby’s window your biggest silent wave.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Subscribe and come back for our next story.
